record.original_question: How can one explicitly construct solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations that either blow up in finite time or remain globally regular, so that the possibility of finite-time singularity formation from smooth initial data can be tested directly rather than only indirectly through a priori estimates?

evidence.quote: How can we build explicitly blowing up or not solutions of Navier-Stokes equations?

Conjecture 5.3. From the discussion of questions 3.1 and 3.2, we can think that a solution to the Millennium problem would be to show that it is always possible to construct mathematically a solution that diverges in a finite time, following the cascade behavior (above), apart from some specific initial conditions like small initial data where the global regularity is ensured.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ (or on the three-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^3$):
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u - \nu\Delta u + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,$$
with viscosity $\nu>0$, where $u(t,x)\in\mathbb{R}^3$ is the velocity field and $p(t,x)\in\mathbb{R}$ the pressure, subject to a smooth, divergence-free initial datum $u_0$ of finite kinetic energy.

Provide an explicit construction (e.g., via a closed-form ansatz, a self-similar profile, a cascade-type iterative scheme, or any other concrete analytic/algorithmic procedure) of solutions of these equations exhibiting either of the following behaviors:

(a) Finite-time singularity: a smooth divergence-free initial datum $u_0$ together with an explicit solution $u(t,x)$ such that there exists $T^*<\infty$ with
$$\limsup_{t\to T^{*-}}\|u(t,\cdot)\|_{L^\infty}=\infty \quad\text{or}\quad \limsup_{t\to T^{*-}}\|\nabla u(t,\cdot)\|_{L^\infty}=\infty;$$

(b) Global regularity: a smooth divergence-free initial datum $u_0$ (not in the small-data perturbative regime) together with an explicit solution $u(t,x)\in C^\infty([0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^3)$ remaining smooth for all $t\ge 0$.

The objective is a constructive, explicit answer—rather than one obtained only through a priori estimates—that directly demonstrates whether finite-time singularity formation from smooth initial data is possible.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a constructive form of the Navier-Stokes global regularity question, one of the Clay Millennium Problems, which remains open as of 2026. While significant recent progress has been made on related questions (e.g., non-uniqueness of weak solutions by Buckmaster–Vicol, finite-time blow-up for Navier-Stokes with forcing by Albritton–Brué–Colombo, and numerical evidence of potential singularities by Hou and collaborators), no explicit construction of either a finite-time singular smooth solution or a globally regular non-perturbative solution to the standard 3D Navier-Stokes equations has been established.

status_evidence.claim: The 3D Navier-Stokes regularity problem is open.

status_evidence.title: Albritton, Brué, Colombo, Non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the forced Navier-Stokes equations
status_evidence.snippet: We construct non-unique Leray solutions of the forced Navier-Stokes equations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress is on forced or weak settings, not explicit blow-up from smooth data without forcing.
